sections.h2: What does the Warren County Clerk do for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
The Warren County Clerk keeps the land records for Bowling Green and the rest of the county, which means the deed that moves your house to a buyer is filed here. The office lists three main services: elections, motor vehicles and public land records. It also issues marriage licenses, commissions notaries and handles delinquent property taxes.

  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102.
  • Phone: (270) 842-9416. Fax for legal recording: (270) 843-5319.
  • Hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Deed room: on the bottom floor of the building, with public terminals and a deputy records clerk to help you start a search.

The office describes Warren as the fastest growing county in Kentucky, and the Census estimate of 149,375 residents for July 2025, up 11.0 percent from 2020, fits that description. A busy recording office is worth calling ahead of closing day.

sections.h2: Where must a Kentucky deed be recorded?
sections.html:
It goes to the clerk of the county where the land lies, or where most of it lies if the parcel crosses a line, under KRS 382.110. For a house in Bowling Green or anywhere else in Warren County, that is this office. The statute also tells the clerk not to accept a deed that fails to say where the seller got title.

When the seller took title by a recorded deed, the new deed cites the older one by office, book and page and gives the recording date. A seller who inherited the property must say how and from whom. The statute was last amended effective July 15, 2026, and it also sets a 45 day limit for a lender to record a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What must a Warren County deed contain?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 lists what a clerk looks for, and a deed that leaves one out cannot be lodged for record. A deed drafted by a title attorney will normally carry each of these.

  • The full names and mailing addresses of the grantor and the grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration paid.
  • An in care of address for the tax bill covering the year of transfer.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate signed by both sides that the stated price is the full price, or for a gift, a certificate that says so and gives an estimated fair cash value.

If the house passes by will or without one, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk of every county holding the estate's land, listing who receives each property and its value. Clerks do not search titles, and the Warren office says it cannot tell you whether liens exist, so a title company handles that step.

sections.h2: What does Warren County charge to record real estate documents?
sections.html:
The clerk posts a Kentucky recording fee schedule, dated January 1, 2020, on its fees and vendors page. Most items add $3.00 for every page after the fifth. A mortgage and a release of mortgage instead add $5.00 per page after the thirtieth.

Selected Warren County recording fees, from the County Clerk's posted schedule
DocumentFirst pages
Deed$50
Deed of correction$46
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Power of attorney$50
Plat$50
Will$47
Lis pendens notice$46

Copies cost less. Printing from a terminal is $.50 a page, a certified copy is $5 for the first three pages plus $.50 for each added page, and a large plat copy is $3. Confirm the total with the office before mailing a package.

sections.h2: How much Kentucky transfer tax does a Warren County seller owe?
sections.html:
The tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value, or part of $500, and the grantor named in the deed owes it. The clerk works out the amount and collects it before the deed is accepted, under KRS 142.050. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the work and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months.

Value means the full price including any liens, or for a gift the estimated open market price. Two worked examples show the rounding:

  • At $258,000, the Census median for an owner occupied Warren County home, the deed holds exactly 516 blocks of $500, so the tax is $258.00.
  • At $312,400 the last block is partial, which makes 625 blocks and a tax of $312.50.

Many transfers are exempt, among them deeds that only provide or release security for a debt, foreclosure deeds, deeds between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, sales for delinquent taxes, partitions, and transfers between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild for nominal consideration. Ask the clerk about any exemption before the deed goes in, since the exemption must fit the statute's wording.

sections.h2: How do I search Warren County land records?
sections.html:
You can search in the deed room or online through eCCLIX, a subscription service run by a records vendor. A private user who searches for personal reasons can run up to five searches a day for free, and commercial users pay a subscription. The index is built on party names and document types, so the address will not find a deed.

If you only know the address, look up the owner on the PVA's website first, and then search by name. Staff will show you how to navigate the system, though they cannot do the search for you.

The clerk also offers DocAlert, a free service from the records vendor that emails you when a mortgage or deed is filed in your name. A homeowner who is selling, or who owns a rental that sits empty, can use it to catch fraudulent filings. Electronic recording is available through four vendors:

  • Simplifile, (800) 460-5657
  • CSC, (866) 652-0111
  • ePN, (888) 325-3365
  • Hopdox, (385) 501-5103 ext. 010

sections.h2: What does the clerk do about delinquent property taxes?
sections.html:
The sheriff sends and collects the bill, but the clerk receives what is unpaid on April 15 and collects it after that. The clerk keeps accepting payments until the annual sale and posts a PDF list of the current delinquent bills. The 2026 sale was scheduled for August 26, 2026 at the clerk's office on East 10th Avenue, and that date has passed.

Ask the clerk for a payoff figure before closing. A bill that moves to delinquency collects 1 percent interest a month along with clerk and attorney commissions, and the lien follows the land for up to 11 years. For a seller who inherited a house with tax arrears, the clerk's office is the place to confirm the exact balance.

sections.h2: What else in Warren County can affect a closing?
sections.html:
Housing costs more here than in Trimble County ($172,000) or Union County ($104,500). The Census puts the Warren median home value at $258,000, median gross rent at $1,002, and the owner occupied rate at 55.6 percent, so rental houses are common. The county issued 1,453 building permits in 2025.

Permits matter at closing. Warren County's Division for Building Services, at 1141 State Street, handles permits outside Bowling Green and Oakland, and states that all new construction needs one. Sheds starting at 120 square feet and all pools need permits as well. Bowling Green has its own building inspector.

A seller with unfinished work, a tenant, a probate problem or back taxes can sell as is to a cash buyer rather than finish repairs before listing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Warren County?
faqs.a: Record it with the Warren County Clerk, whose mailing address is P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102. You can also record electronically through Simplifile, CSC, ePN or Hopdox.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Warren County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $50, plus $3.00 for every page after the fifth. A deed of correction is $46. The transfer tax is separate and is paid by the seller.

faqs.q: Can I search Warren County deeds by address?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's index is built on party names and document types. Look up the owner by address on the PVA website, then search the clerk's records by that name.

faqs.q: Does the Warren County Clerk run a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff can show you how to use the system, but they cannot conduct a title search or confirm whether liens exist. A title company or attorney does that.

faqs.q: Who pays the Kentucky transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The grantor named in the deed pays it, at fifty cents per $500 of value. The County Clerk collects it before recording the deed.
